Research on the United States shows that large-scale warming and land–atmosphere feedbacks drive increases in extreme heat. In general, research shows that such heat raises electricity demand and stresses energy systems. In general, research shows that extreme heat and wind raise the chance of ignitions near power lines. These are general drivers of dangerous heat-index days, not findings specific to Virginia.
